reviewMethod: Provisional assistant visual inspection using local OpenCV (cv2.setNumThreads(1)): 16 timestamped RGB samples spanning each of 102 clips (0.1 seconds through duration minus 0.1), read as real contact sheets with view_image. For 20 candidate windows, sequentially decoded the first four seconds and retained 32 evenly spaced timestamped frames from 0 through approximately 4 seconds, visually inspected with view_image; 12 windows retained. No continuous playback or full-frame-by-frame inspection; no audio review. Only explicit 0-4 second source spans are labelled normal; unknown tails remain unannotated.
limitations: Assistant visual screening is provisional, not human ground truth. Brief events between sampled timestamps cannot be excluded, even in the denser 32-frame windows.
Sequential decoding to obtain samples does not mean all decoded frames were visually inspected. No claim of continuous motion inspection.
No identity, intent, relationship, injury, crime or audio judgments. Handshake/greeting descriptions concern visible hand-clasp configurations only.
Settings are descriptive, not proof of actor/session independence. Every accepted clip remains in the single unresolved VID V2 training cohort; no calibration or holdout split is authorized.
Consent is author-reported; no independently verified participant-release or complete-rights-clearance claim.
102 of 378 newly imported recordings were screened. The other 276 remain pending, not normal by inference from publisher labels.

No perimeter-computer-lab match was found among the 102 samples. Courtyard/corridor campus settings match descriptively; the three portrait classroom clips broadly match educational interiors but not the exact lab, camera framing or background.

Only twelve 4-second normal spans are retained. No label extrapolation to clip tails; vague gesture-only scenes, unresolved physical interaction, prop-centred scenes and unmatched backgrounds were omitted.
